subtitle: A Jain Queen in a Changing Hoysala World

panels.shot: epic wide of Shantala Devi standing between Belur temple towers and Chandragiri hill, dusk light dividing the frame
panels.action: Shantala Devi stands poised on a stone terrace, one hand toward the ornate Belur temple, the other toward the stark hill of Shravanabelagola, her face calm yet resolute in the fading light.

dialogue.text: In an age when Hoysalas turned to new gods and new wars, Queen Shantala Devi walked a different path—writing her Jain faith into stone, and choosing her own final fast.

i18n.hi: जब होयसला नए देवता और नई जंगों की ओर मुड़े, रानी शांतला देवी ने अलग राह चुनी—अपनी जैन आस्था पत्थरों पर लिख दी, और अपना अंतिम उपवास खुद चुना।

panels.shot: slow aerial drift over Malnad hills and river valleys at sunrise
panels.action: Morning mist curls over green hills and river valleys of early 12th-century Karnataka, scattered shrines and fortified towns dotting the landscape beneath a pale sun.

dialogue.text: The Hoysala realm wakes in the early 1100s—hill forts in the Malnad, temple towns in the plains, Jain basadis and Shaiva and Vaishnava shrines sharing the same red earth.

i18n.hi: ११वीं सदी के शुरू में होयसला राज्य जागता है—मालनाड की पहाड़ी किलें, मैदानों के मंदिर नगर, जैन बसदी, शैव और वैष्णव देवालय एक ही लाल मिट्टी बाँटते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Hoysala court at Dvarasamudra, king on throne, courtiers arrayed
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall at Dvarasamudra, King Vishnuvardhana sits on a low throne, generals and ministers gathered as sculptors present carved stone panels for approval.

dialogue.text: Vishnuvardhana, Hoysala king, pushes his frontier against the Cholas and celebrates with stone—commissioning temples at Belur and Dvarasamudra, filling their walls with stories in soapstone.

i18n.hi: होयसला नरेश विष्णुवर्धन चोलों की सीमा तक धकेलता है और पत्थरों से जश्न मनाता है—बेलूर और द्वारसमुद्र में मंदिर बनवाता है, साबुन पत्थर की दीवारों पर कहानियाँ उकेरता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shantala Devi in the royal hall, slightly apart from the court
panels.action: Shantala Devi sits slightly to one side of the throne on a carved seat, hands folded, observing the court with composed eyes, her jewelry and garments rich but understated.

dialogue.text: Beside him sits his mahadevi, Shantala Devi. Inscriptions name her not as shadow, but with lineage, grants, devotion, and a voice of her own.

i18n.hi: उसके पास उसकी महादेवी शांतला देवी बैठती है। शिलालेख उसे परछाईं नहीं, बल्कि वंश, अनुदान, भक्ति और अपनी आवाज़ वाली रानी के रूप में दर्ज करते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Shantala Devi’s hands and veena, soft light from a lattice window
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Shantala Devi’s slender fingers rest on the strings of a veena, the instrument lying across her lap as she looks out toward the temple town in thought.

dialogue.text: One record calls her a master of music and dance. It is praise, not gossip. We do not see her perform, but we hear echoes of skill that impressed her age.

i18n.hi: एक लेख उसे संगीत और नृत्य की सिद्धहस्त बताता है। यह प्रशंसा है, गप नहीं। हम उसे नाचते नहीं देखते, पर कौशल की गूँज सुनते हैं जिसने उसके समय को चकित किया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Belur temple courtyard bustling with artisans, Shantala Devi arriving in palanquin
panels.action: Artisans carve friezes in the bustling courtyard of the Chennakesava complex at Belur as Shantala Devi steps down from a palanquin, attendants around her, eyes drawn to a smaller shrine rising nearby.

dialogue.text: At Belur, the great Vaishnava temple grows. Yet nearby a more modest shrine, Kappe Chennigaraya, carries her name—one of several works linked to her patronage.

i18n.hi: बेलूर में महान वैष्णव मंदिर उठता है। पर पास ही छोटा सा कप्पे चन्निगराया मंदिर उसका नाम रखता है—उसकी संरक्षिका से जुड़े कई कामों में से एक।

panels.shot: low-angle view of Shantala Devi examining stone panels, sculptors nearby
panels.action: Shantala Devi leans forward to study an unfinished sculpture panel, a sculptor standing respectfully by, chisels in hand, while other workers pause to watch her judgment.

dialogue.text: She moves among sculptors, not as mere observer, but as donor. Inscriptions show royal women choosing sites, endowments, and the very gods their gifts would serve.

i18n.hi: वह शिल्पियों के बीच चलती है, सिर्फ दर्शक नहीं, बल्कि दानदाता बनकर। अभिलेख दिखाते हैं कि राजमहिलाएँ खुद स्थल, दान और उन देवों को चुनती हैं जिनकी सेवा के लिए वे देती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Jain basadi, Shantala Devi before a Jina image
panels.action: Within a simple stone Jain basadi, Shantala Devi kneels before a serene seated Jina image, lamp flames gently lighting her face and the polished stone.

dialogue.text: Yet inside her, another thread runs clear. In Shravanabelagola and other records she appears as a Jain donor, placing gifts before Jinas, guided by a Jain acharya.

i18n.hi: पर उसके भीतर एक और धारा साफ बहती है। श्रवणबेलगोला और दूसरे लेख उसे जैन दानदाता दिखाते हैं, जो जिनों के आगे दान रखती है, एक जैन आचार्य से मार्गदर्शन पाती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Shantala Devi listening to Jain guru Prabhachandra (shown only as robed figure)
panels.action: Shantala Devi sits on a stone floor, attentive, as an elderly Jain monk in simple robes gestures in calm instruction, other women seated behind her.

dialogue.text: Her inscription names Prabhachandra Siddhanta Deva as guru. Under his guidance she supports Jain establishments, while her husband’s court leans strongly toward Vaishnava temples.

i18n.hi: उसके लेख में प्रभाचंद्र सिद्धांत देवा का नाम गुरु के रूप में है। उनके मार्गदर्शन में वह जैन संस्थानों को सहारा देती है, जबकि उसके पति का दरबार दृढ़ता से वैष्णव मंदिरों की ओर झुकता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Halebidu twin temple complex, one side subtly associated with Shantala
panels.action: The twin temple complex at Dvarasamudra rises, one half dedicated to Hoysalesvara, the other to Shantalesvara, with Shantala Devi standing in the foreground, watching the stone towers pierce the sky.

dialogue.text: At Dvarasamudra, the Shantalesvara shrine bears her name. Again, stone remembers a queen whose agency was strong enough to be shared in the main temple form.

i18n.hi: द्वारसमुद्र में शांतलेश्वर मंदिर उसका नाम रखता है। फिर पत्थर एक ऐसी रानी को याद करता है जिसकी शक्ति मुख्य मंदिर रूप में भी साझी की गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shantala Devi at a court grant ceremony, scribes writing on palm-leaf
panels.action: In the audience hall, Shantala Devi dictates to scribes seated with palm-leaf bundles, while a small group of Jain monks and temple officials stand by awaiting the formal grant.

dialogue.text: Record my gift, so that even after me, the lamps will not go dark.

i18n.hi: मेरे दान को लिख लो, ताकि मेरे बाद भी दीप कभी बुझें नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on palm-leaf manuscript being inscribed, Shantala Devi faintly reflected in a metal vessel
panels.action: A stylus scratches script onto a palm leaf; in a polished metal vessel nearby, Shantala Devi’s face appears faint, watching the act of writing that will carry her name.

dialogue.text: We know her from such words. Epigraphia Carnatica preserves these grants, where her name stands beside villages, tanks, and income set aside for Jain worship and service.

i18n.hi: हम उसे ऐसे शब्दों से पहचानते हैं। ‘एपिग्राफ़िया कार्नाटिका’ इन दानों को सँभालती है, जहाँ उसका नाम गाँवों, तालाबों और जैन पूजा व सेवा के लिए रखी आय के साथ खड़ा है।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of Belur temple, Shantala Devi walking past Vaishnava icons
panels.action: Shantala Devi walks through the cool interior of the Belur temple, rows of Vaishnava icons glowing in lamplight as priests perform rituals and she passes by with quiet respect.

dialogue.text: Shantala Devi lives in a plural house. She does not renounce her Jain faith to match her husband; instead she inhabits a court where multiple religious currents run side by side.

i18n.hi: शांतला देवी बहु-धर्मी घर में जीती है। वह अपने पति के लिए अपनी जैन आस्था नहीं छोड़ती; वह ऐसे दरबार में रहती है जहाँ कई धार्मिक धाराएँ साथ-साथ बहती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of aging Shantala Devi on Chandragiri hill, gazing at Gommateshwara in distance
panels.action: An older Shantala Devi, lines of age on her face, sits on a stone ledge atop Chandragiri hill, looking across the valley toward the towering Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola.

dialogue.text: By 1131, her path nears its end. On Chandragiri hill at Shravanabelagola, she prepares for sallekhana—the Jain fast unto death, undertaken as a final act of discipline and detachment.

i18n.hi: ११३१ तक उसकी राह अंत के करीब पहुँचती है। श्रवणबेलगोला के चंद्रगिरि पर्वत पर वह सल्लेखना की तैयारी करती है—मरण तक जैन उपवास, जो अंतिम अनुशासन और विरक्ति का संकल्प है।

panels.shot: close-up on Shantala Devi’s calm face as she begins the fast, sky behind her
panels.action: Shantala Devi sits in meditation posture, her eyes half-closed, lips faintly curved in inner peace as the open sky stretches behind her with soft clouds.

dialogue.text: May this body fade softly, and may my vows remain steady.

i18n.hi: यह देह धीरे-धीरे हल्की हो जाए, और मेरे व्रत अटल रहें।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of stone inscription being carved on Chandragiri, Shantala seated in background
panels.action: A stonecutter carefully chisels Kannada script into a rock face on Chandragiri, while in the blurred background Shantala Devi sits still in meditation, attendants watching solemnly.

dialogue.text: As she fasts, her life is carved into stone—the Chandragiri inscription noting her family, her guru, her gifts, and this chosen manner of passing from the world.

i18n.hi: जब वह उपवास करती है, उसका जीवन पत्थर पर दर्ज होता है—चंद्रगिरि लेख उसके कुल, उसके गुरु, उसके दान और संसार से यह चुना हुआ विदा लेख में बाँधता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Chandragiri hill at dusk, Shantala small against sweeping landscape
panels.action: The sun sets behind Chandragiri hill, Shantala Devi’s seated figure now small against the vast slope, while monks and attendants stand at a respectful distance around her.

dialogue.text: Her death, like her life, is recorded plainly. No later legend of conversion or conflict replaces the simple fact: a Jain queen remained Jain to the end.

i18n.hi: उसकी मृत्यु भी, उसकी जीवन की तरह, साफ-साफ लिखी है। बाद की कोई कथा न रूपांतरण की, न टकराव की, इस सरल सच्चाई को बदलती है: एक जैन रानी अंत तक जैन ही रही।

panels.shot: slow push-in on weathered Chandragiri inscription, letters worn but legible
panels.action: The camera moves closer to a weathered rock face, its chiselled letters softened by time yet still legible, surrounded by dry grass and wind-swept stone.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars like S. Settar read those lines again, seeing there one of medieval Karnataka’s clearest records of a queen’s agency and spiritual choice.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, एस. सेत्तार जैसे विद्वान उन पंक्तियों को फिर पढ़ते हैं, और वहाँ मध्यमकालीन कर्नाटक में रानी की स्वतंत्रता और आध्यात्मिक चुनाव का सबसे स्पष्ट लेख देखते हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot blending Belur temple and Chandragiri hill in one composition, Shantala as faint overlay
panels.action: Belur’s sculpted towers and Chandragiri’s bare hill share the frame under a vast sky, with a faint, translucent image of Shantala Devi overlaid, eyes steady, between the two worlds she bridged.

dialogue.text: Shantala Devi’s story reminds us that even inside powerful courts, integrity can persist—quiet, inscribed in grants and stone, holding its faith while kingdoms shift around it.

i18n.hi: शांतला देवी की कथा याद दिलाती है कि ताक़तवर दरबारों के बीच भी सत्यनिष्ठा टिक सकती है—शांत, दानों और पत्थरों में लिखी, अपना विश्वास थामे हुए जबकि राज्य उसके चारों ओर बदलते रहते हैं।

title_i18n.hi: शांतला देवी अपना विश्वास निभाती है

subtitle_i18n.en: A Jain Queen in a Changing Hoysala World
subtitle_i18n.hi: बदलती होयसला दुनिया में एक जैन रानी
